Effect of Encryption Upgrade in 25.10 and Later

The 25.10 Monthly Update includes an upgrade to the encryption used by Siebel CRM. This will require brief downtime—that is, Rolling Updates will not work when crossing the 25.10 boundary . Please review the links for the feature _AES 256 Replacement Using OpenSSL_ below.

Required Downloads

Each Monthly Update patch available on My Oracle Support is divided into a series of archive (ZIP) files. Depending on the Siebel Application Server operating system and the features you wish to deploy, you do not need to download all the files associated with the Monthly Update. Please use the following information to assist in selecting the files that you must download.
The ZIP files provided in the Monthly Update will all have a name of the form p___.zip, where:
- refers to the MOS patch number for the Monthly Update. It will be an eight-digit number, such as 37386170.
- refers to the Monthly Update’s release in the form YYM, without a separator, such as “263” for 26.3.
- refers to one of the supported platforms:

Update Basics
A Monthly Update provides new product features and available fixes. Beyond this document, please review these related items:

- Installation instructions: For more about this Siebel CRM Update, including instructions for preparing the product media and for installing Siebel CRM, see the latest version of the _Installation Guide_ in _Siebel Bookshelf_ from the Siebel CRM Documentation site.
- Third-Party Certifications: For a list of Third-Party Certifications, please visit My Oracle Support and search for “Siebel Industry Applications” on the _Certifications_ tab.
- FAQ: The Siebel CRM Continuous Release Model (Doc ID 2378034.1).

NOTE: This document contains two years (24 months) of rolling content. For bug fixes and known issues in versions released before the scope of this document, please download earlier versions from Oracle Support (DOC ID 2382435.1).
Back to top
Repository Updates

Some features require Repository, Seed, or Manifest changes in order to take advantage of the feature. These changes must be imported through execution of the _RepositoryUpdate_ utility in the Development environment. Please refer to the _Database Upgrade Guide_ for information on how to use RepositoryUpdate.
NOTE: Not all features require Repository changes. Examine the “Repository Update Required” column in the New Features tables below to see if such changes are required for a particular feature.
Back to top

Additional Background Changes to database schema objects is performed using "Data Definition Language" (DDL). When DDL is provided upon an existing object (such as a change to a column definition) or to create certain kinds of new objects (such as indexes), the traditional approach that the

notes: field_0:Description=NOTE: Full Runtime Repository Migration will leverage this feature to avoid changes required to modify schema objects, b

text: various Siebel CRM utilities have used could introduce "table locks" or other conditions that would block end users from being able to use the application while the DDL was executing. When this occurred, downtime could occur during the application of Siebel Updates (PostInstallDBSetup or RepositoryUpgrade) and Migration operations.
Basic Technical Information

By modifying our existing utilities to leverage built-in capabilities of modern versions of the Oracle and Microsoft SQL Server database platforms, we can execute DDL that accomplishes the same end result without forcing downtime.
- For Oracle platforms, we leverage the DBMS_REDEFINITION package to make changes to objects without making any schema objects offline.
- For Microsoft SQL Server platforms, we leverage the "ONLINE" keyword to modify objects without bringing any schema objects offline.
For more information on the technical details of these database-level capabilities, please refer to the Oracle or Microsoft documentation as appropriate.
NOTE: This change is not applicable to either DB2 database platform.

field_1: Replacement of Obsolete Data Types from Oracle and MSSQL Databases | Training on this feature is available onOracle University.: This feature provides a utility to convert obsolete Column types, such as Oracle's LONG and Microsoft SQL Server's TEXT/NTEXT to their modern equivalents: CLOBs and VARCHAR(max)/NVARCHAR(max). The driver behind this is that the respective database vendors deprecated these data types a number of years ago and modern database engines are no longer being optimized for these older types. Replacing them with their modern equivalents will take advantage of their inherent benefits, such as greater data storage space, as well as future-proofing should either vendor ever elect to completely end support for these. | field_3: • Database Upgrade Guide • Business Process Framework: Workfow Guide • Confguring Siebel Business Applications • Integration Platform Technologies: Siebel Enterprise Application Integration Guide | field_4: No

Instructions for 38779291--Fixed an issue to publish Operation field in Integration component.
_Background_

User creation via the _User_ Integration Component of the _Users_ Integration Object fails as the Open API specification for the Integration Object does not have a required field _operation_ . This is because the _operation_ field is marked as a “system” field in the _User_ Integration Component definition, while the Siebel Open API specification only includes the fields that marked as “data”. To ensure the _operation_ field is included in the Open API specification, it must be changed to a Data field.
_Steps_
Repository Changes
Perform the following changes to convert the _operation_ field from “system” to “data”:
1. Select the _Users_ Integration Object.
2. Select the child Integration Component _User_ .
3. Select the child Integration Component Field _operation_ .
4. Modify the Type attribute to “Data”.
New Features and Bug Fixes in Siebel CRM Monthly Update 26.1
New Features in Siebel CRM 26.1

Feature Name: Preserve Customer Configuration Changes During Monthly Updates | Description: This feature decreases the time and effort to uptake new features released in Monthly Updates. Effective with this feature, the RepositoryUpgrade process has been replaced with "RepositoryUpdate". This new process reduces the number of changes made by the utility, with an overall benefit of a smoother uptake of the content introduced in a Siebel Monthly Update, allowing customers to leverage new features more easily than before. Background Formerly, during a Monthly Update, there was a process known as "RepositoryUpgrade", which updated the Siebel CRM environment to incorporate Repository changes, schema changes, seed data, and other modifications introduced by new features. This utility delivered optional Repository changes made by the Oracle Siebel CRM development team. During execution, the RepositoryUpgrade utility imported data from the intervening releases since the last time it was run. If the Siebel CRM environment was not kept up- to-date regularly with the latest Siebel CRM Monthly Updates, then the number of Repository changes that must be applied increased as well, | Documentation: • Database Upgrade Guide | Repository Update Required?: No
